svg.text: Aperture OS demo — ESP32 wiring (8 wires + 2 indicator LEDs)
Pi pins are BCM GPIO; (pin N) is the physical header position. 3.3 V logic only. 330 Ω–1 kΩ resistor in series on every signal wire. Wire with both boards powered off.
ESP32 powered by its own USB charger / power bank.
Never from a Pi GPIO. USB data cable unplugged
during the run (only plug in to flash).
GPIO14 TXD → ESP32 GPIO16 RX2 (spare, optional)
GPIO15 RXD ← ESP32 GPIO17 TX2 telemetry 115200
GPIO23 ← ESP32 GPIO21 safety readback (+ LED)
GND → breadboard GND rail (shared with Pi pin 6)
GPIO19 → Pi GPIO22 (pin 15) actuator output + LED to GND
GPIO21 → Pi GPIO23 (pin 16) safety-relay output + LED to GND
GPIO17 TX2 → Pi GPIO15 (pin 10) JSON telemetry
GPIO16 RX2 ← Pi GPIO14 (pin 8) spare, can skip
5V / USB ← own USB charger or power bank
Indicator LEDs (so judges can see the bug)
On each ESP32 output, add an LED in parallel with the wire to the Pi:
FIRMWARE LIED moment: telemetry says safety=0,
but the GPIO21 LED stays lit and Pi GPIO23 reads HIGH.
LED long leg (+) toward the ESP32, short leg to GND.
1× Raspberry Pi (3/4/Zero 2 W) + SD card + PSU
1× USB charger / power bank for the ESP32
Pi setup: enable UART, disable serial console on /dev/serial0 (raspi-config).
